MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE LOMITA CITY COUNCIL
July 15, 2013

1.  OPENING CEREMONIES

a.  Call Meeting to Order

A regular meeting of the Lomita City Council was called to order at 7:00 p.m., on Monday, July
15, 2013, in the Council Chambers, at Lomita City Hall, 24300 Narbonne Avenue.

b.  Flag Salute

Councilmember Savidan led the salute to the flag.

c.  Invocation

Councilmember Traina gave the invocation.

d.  Roll Call

Those responding to roll call by Assistant City Clerk Shumway were COUNCILMEMBERS:
Gazeley, Traina, Sanchez, Savidan, and Mayor Estrada. Also present were City Manager Rock,
Assistant City Manager Sugano, City Attorney Hogin, Public Works Director Damasse,
Community Services Director McPherron, Administrative Services Director Chavez, Parks and
Recreation Director Harding, and Assistant City Clerk Shumway.

2.  APPROVAL OF AGENDA

Councilmember Gazeley moved to approve the agenda. Councilmember Savidan seconded the
motion, which carried unanimously.

3.  SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS

Jacki Bacharach, Executive Director of the South Bay Cities Council of Government (SBCCG),
presented the City of Lomita with a platinum award, and thanked Alicia Velasco and Michael
Sansbury for their hard work on the Energy Leader Partnership Program. According to Ms.
Bacharach the City saw significant savings, of $22,000, through incentives and rebates as a
result of the Energy Leader Partnership Program. Scott Gobble, Southern California Edison
Regional Manager, congratulated the City of Lomita on its energy efficiency and savings, and
added that the City is the first to receive the platinum award in the South Bay.

Mayor Gazeley thanked Jacki Bacharach for her efforts in making sure that Measure R Highway
Funds were not allocated to the Crenshaw/LAX Transit Corridor Metro Project, but rather
remained as intended in the South Bay Highway Program Fund.

Mayor Estrada and Councilmembers presented certificates of recognition to the Dancemark
Studio dancers, choreographer, and owner for winning the Grand Champion Award.

Mayor Estrada and Councilmembers congratulated Gia Stokes on being appointed to the
Planning Commission.

  Page 1
 4. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

City Manager Rock informed those in attendance that the Cypress Water Production Facility
(CWPF) has been working well for three months, and that the current blend ratio is 65/35
(Metropolitan water to treated well water). City Manager Rock did note that a higher percentage
of the Metropolitan Water is currently coming from the Colorado River vs. the State Project
Water, which has higher hardness levels. City Manager Rock also stated that the City's new
water treatment operator is now operating CWPF, while Water Works is now on a retainer
contract.

5.  ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

David Popelka, Planning Commissioner, urged residents to vote in the upcoming election, and
also asked City Council to work together.

Rob Friedrich, Lomita resident, stated that the TDS levels are high in Lomita’s water.

Scott Gobble, Southern California Edison Regional Manager, provided Council with emergency
notification packets that contain the contract information to be used in case of emergency.

In response to Councilmember Gazeley’s question about underground power lines from wind
farms, Scott Gobble stated that the Public Utility Commission made a decision last week to
place 3.9 miles of power lines from wind farms underground, at a total project cost of $224
million. Mr. Gobble added that the project could be delayed until 2015, so given the closure of
the San Onofre plant, energy conservation is quite important. In regards to power outages, Mr.
Gobble stated that currently heat levels are normal, so things should be fine this summer, but he
did urge the public to watch for power alerts and to conserve energy.

6. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS AND MEETING ATTENDANCE REPORTS FROM THE CITY
  COUNCIL

In response to Councilmember Traina’s question as to whether the City has a plan to feed zone
2, Director Damasse responded that there are currently no plans to do that at this time.

Responding to Councilmember Traina’s questions regarding the water hardness levels being
above the established range, Director Damasse stated that increase in water hardness was due
to the Metropolitan Water District receiving higher percentages of water from the Colorado
River instead of from the State Water Project (which currently has hardness levels of 250-280).

Councilmember Sanchez thanked Alicia Velasco for her hard work on the Energy Leader
Partnership Program, and for achieving the platinum award for the City. Councilmember
Sanchez also stated that water hardness was between 270 and 280, which is within the
established range.

Councilmember Savidan complemented the staff at CWPF, and also stated how clean the facility
was.

Councilmember Gazeley informed those in attendance that five dead crows had been found in
Lomita, and warned residents to take precautions regarding the West Nile Virus.

  Page 2
 Councilmember Gazeley also invited those in attendance to IRWU’s Second Annual Texas
Hold’em Poker Tournament, which will take place on July 30, 2013, at 6 p.m. at the Normandie
Casino; Councilmember Gazeley also noted that the proceeds will benefit childhood cancer
research.

Mayor Estrada thanked Alicia Velasco and Michael Sansbury for their hard work and for the
savings they achieved for the City.

7. CONSENT AGENDA

Councilmember Sanchez asked to pull Item 7.D. from the Consent Agenda. Councilmember
Gazeley moved to approve the Consent Agenda, minus Item 7.D. Councilmember Savidan
seconded the motion, which carried unanimously.

Item 7.D. - In response to Councilmember Sanchez’s question as to whether there is a
differentiation between commercial vehicles and vehicles for personal use, and whether
commercial vehicles would be cited, Community Services Director McPherron stated that there
is no distinction between commercial and personal use vehicles, and that in accordance with the
proposed ordinance, citations will be issued based on the three-dimensional parameters/size of
the vehicle. Director McPherron also added that the goal was to identify vehicles based on the
size, and not leave it in the hands of enforcement officials to determine whether vehicles are in
compliance or not with the ordinance.

City Attorney Hogin clarified that creating a standard which differentiates identification and
determination of commercial versus residential writing on vehicles could be a violation of the first
amendment.

Councilmember Savidan recommended including weekends among the citable days, as that
particular exemption allows oversized vehicle on City streets almost 50% of the time.
Furthermore, Councilmember Savidan suggested increasing the hours for enforcement to 24/7,
instead of just 2 a.m. to 6 a.m.

Councilmember Savidan moved to send the oversized vehicle ordinance back to staff for review
so that they can incorporate some of the previously discussed recommendations.
Councilmember Sanchez seconded the motion, which carried unanimously.

In response to Councilmember Traina’s question on how the criteria regarding size was
established, Director McPherron stated that there is no uniform standard, and that criteria was
established based on a recommendation from City Council.

  a. Motion to Waive Further Reading

  b. Recommendation to approve the minutes for the Regular City Council Meeting held on
  July 1, 2013. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

  c. Approval of Demands

  d. Approval of an Ordinance adding Article 3 (Overnight Parking of Oversized Vehicles and
  Trailers) to Title VIII, Chapter 1 of the Lomita Municipal Code to add requirements for the
  parking of oversized vehicles and trailers, adopting resolution establishing the oversized

   permit issuance fee and adopting resolution establishing the fines for the offense of the
  ordinance violation parking penalty. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

  e. Award of a Public Works contract to All American Asphalt in the amount of $928,000 for the
  Crenshaw Blvd./Lomita Blvd. Intersection and Lomita Blvd. Pavement Rehabilitation
  Project. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

SCHEDULED ITEMS:

8. HOME ENERGY RETROFIT OPPORTUNITY (HERO) PROGRAM PARTICIPATION

Assistant City Manager Sugano stated that the HERO Program was developed as a turnkey
program to save California jurisdictions time and resources in developing a standalone program
that allows property owners to enter into contractual assessments to finance the installation of
renewable energy, energy efficiency, and/or water conservation improvements on their property.
According to Assistant City Manager Sugano, the improvements will be financed by the
issuance of bonds from the Western Riverside Council of Governments, and that participation in
the program will be 100% voluntary.

Councilmember Gazeley added that the HERO Program provides Lomita residents with an
opportunity to make improvements to their properties even if they do not have funds right now;
Councilmember Gazeley stated that the repayment terms would be within 20 years. In
response to Councilmember Traina’s question as to whether the obligation stays with the
property or the owner, Councilmember Gazeley responded that it stays with the property, which
has not been a problem in Riverside.

Councilmember Gazeley moved to approve the City’s participation in the HERO Program.
Councilmember Savidan seconded the motion, which carried unanimously.

ADJOURNMENT

Meeting adjourned in memory of Pete Giacomi and Ernest Roach at 7:41 p.m.

Respectfully Submitted,

__________________________________
Lena Shumway, Assistant City Clerk, CMC
